zh: 网格上每步代价相同，最少步数就是 BFS 距离。所有最短路上的每一步都从距离 d 的格子走到距离 d+1 的格子，这些边构成一个有向无环图。
在 BFS 的同时做 DP：best[格子] 表示沿最短路到达该格最多能捡到的宝藏数，只从距离恰好小 1 的邻格转移。
起点 best=起点是否有宝藏；BFS 弹出格子 u 时检查四个邻格 z（不越界、不是墙）：z 未访问则 dist[z]=dist[u]+1、best[z]=best[u]+[z 有宝藏] 并入队；若 dist[z]==dist[u]+1 则用 best[u]+[z 有宝藏] 更新 best[z] 的最大值。出口不可达输出 -1 0，否则输出 dist[end] 和 best[end]。
en: Every step costs the same on the grid, so the minimum number of steps is the BFS distance. On any shortest path each step goes from a cell at distance d to a cell at distance d + 1, and these edges form a directed acyclic graph.
Run a DP alongside the BFS: best[cell] is the maximum number of treasures collectable on a shortest path to that cell, and it only takes transitions from neighbors whose distance is exactly one less.

Set best at the start to whether the start holds a treasure. When BFS pops a cell u, look at the four neighbors z that are in bounds and not walls: if z is unvisited, set dist[z] = dist[u] + 1, best[z] = best[u] + [z has treasure] and enqueue it; if dist[z] == dist[u] + 1, raise best[z] to best[u] + [z has treasure] if larger. If the exit is unreachable print -1 0, otherwise print dist[end] and best[end].

explanationEn:
## Approach

First run BFS from start to get the shortest distance to every cell; then do DP in increasing order of distance, transitioning only from neighbors whose distance is 1 smaller, and record for each cell the maximum number of treasures over shortest paths that reach it.

## Proof of correctness

With the BFS distances, every edge of a shortest path goes from d to d+1, which forms a directed acyclic graph. Processing in increasing distance, the DP has already considered all shortest-path predecessors, so taking the maximum gives the maximum number of treasures over shortest paths to that cell. The exit's distance and DP value are exactly what is asked.

## Complexity

Time O(rows*cols), space O(rows*cols).
